title: Labyrinth
build: Two-sided English disk edition; stored credit at $743D-$747D includes V 1.0 V; supplied G64 preservation images

records.c: First 256 bytes of the unpacked M1 map resource. In the naturally reached closed-gate snapshot, cells zero through three are $01,$03,$01,$01; the shared classifier uses these for the first four 64-unit horizontal columns. The selected gate example covers world X zero through 255. Other map consumers and rows remain open.

Sixteen low-nibble-to-type entries read by the shared map classifier. Initially entry one maps to type zero and entry three to type fourteen. The gate approach threshold writes type fourteen into entries zero and two when it starts the sequence. These are mutable scene-map semantics, not a pixel collision rectangle.
Three JMP stubs at $8C86/$8C89/$8C8C all target the RTS at $8EA3. The gate normally uses the resident negative-mode map classifier, rather than these alternate classification callbacks.
JMP $8C96, the gate sequence callback invoked from the resident scene/action loop. It handles the gate story stages and the approach-depth condition.
JMP the RTS at $8C95. The per-motion room-update callback has no additional body in this gate overlay; the command/frame callback at $8C8F carries its scripted sequence.
Return from the gate update hook. This one-byte RTS is also the target of the $8C92 jump.

Read gate script stage $8ED3. Negative selects the ordinary waiting/dialogue path at $8CD8. Stages zero and one classify the current map cell through API $0818, change it using $072E through API $081B, request sound three through API $081E, disable the player display slot and set depth $C0 before incrementing the stage. Stage at least two enters $8CC0, which queues the first corridor after a counted delay. The approach threshold is separately described at $8D92; other dialogue helpers remain partially analysed.

Request sound five through API $081E, then call API $0839 with Y four, waiting through four sixty-tick downcounter intervals. Store two in deferred scene byte $02C3, end the current object-sequence flag and increment $8ED3. Resident $59AF later transfers the deferred request into $0530; this does not use the generic $4115 exit dispatcher. Tests keep the original counted-delay loop and intercept only its per-interval wait.

While gate stage is negative, update sound/pose helpers and optional actor movement. Phase $8EB4 at least fourteen goes straight to the approach-depth check. Earlier phases use countdown $8EB5. A negative $030B during phases below seven jumps to phase seven with countdown one and calls $086C. On countdown expiry, phase zero in a nonzero scene skips to phase seven; otherwise phase zero calls $086F and copies up to 28 name bytes from $0504 to $8F22, then appends a period and terminator. $8E09 selects the phase delay and, for phases zero through six, its text. The phase then increments. Effects triggered when countdown reaches one include the phase-seven $0824 call and map changes in phases eleven/twelve. The latch is joystick-port-one fire, traced through $19AE/$1993 and verified live; the complete actor sequence remains open.

Read player depth $0544. Return if its sign bit is set or if it is below $32 (50). Otherwise store zero in gate stage $8ED3 and store type fourteen into mapping entries $073E and $0740. This begins the gate script; there is no horizontal-coordinate comparison inside this routine. Closed-gate map depth limits restrict the approach elsewhere. All 256 depth bytes are tested against this original routine.

Load countdown $8EB5 from $8EC5 indexed by phase $8EB4. For phases zero through six, build text pointer $10/$11 from split tables $8ED4/$8EDB, clear text margin $0342 and call headered-message API $0803. Phases seven and above return after setting the delay. Tests exercise all fourteen scheduled phases.

Decrement $8EB7; on zero reset it to one. Phase zero returns without a pose write. Phases one through seven alternate flag $8EB3, use random API $0821 and signed counters $8EE2 to select pose $8EB8, and write it to $034F. Phases eight through ten take a pose from $8EB9 indexed by phase; later phases retain the selected pose. Visual identities of these pose numbers remain open.
If $0298 equals three, request sound $18 through $081E. Otherwise return with A zero. This routine does not identify the input meaning of $0298.
Signed alternating pose-selection flag read and written by $8E29, also set to one by the phase-seven event. This captured state is $FF.

Shared introduction/gate sequence phase. $8CD8 schedules phases zero through thirteen, then phase fourteen or higher bypasses the sequence countdown and checks approach depth. The natural steady gate capture is phase fourteen.
Eight-bit callback countdown for $8CD8, loaded from $8EC5. It decrements before the zero test, so initial zero wraps to 255. Values are callback counts, not established seconds.
Decremented by $8E29; zero reloads one and permits pose selection on that callback.
Pose number maintained by $8E29 and copied to $034F. Pose artwork meanings remain open.
Fourteen callback-countdown values for phases zero through thirteen: 18,28,24,56,30,42,72,8,8,4,4,4,4,4. $8E09 displays a text only for the first seven phases.
Seven low bytes of headered-message pointers, paired with high bytes at $8EDB. Indexed only for sequence phases below seven by $8E09.
Seven high bytes paired with $8ED4, selecting the messages at $8EF5, $8EFF, $8F1A, $8F40, $8F8A, $8FAE and $8FDE.

Headered sequence message 0, selected through $8ED4/$8EDB by $8E09. Normalized visible text in the captured setup: "You...". The first two bytes are message header fields; inline formatting is interpreted by $67B7.

Headered sequence message 1, selected through $8ED4/$8EDB by $8E09. Normalized visible text in the captured setup: "You in the first row...". The first two bytes are message header fields; inline formatting is interpreted by $67B7.

Headered sequence message 2, selected through $8ED4/$8EDB by $8E09. It addresses the player by name after YOU,. The first two bytes are message header fields; inline formatting is interpreted by $67B7. Phase zero rewrites the name field at $8F22. Published listing data substitutes ANON for the contributor's setup name; original captures remain private in work/.

Headered sequence message 3, selected through $8ED4/$8EDB by $8E09. Normalized visible text in the captured setup: "We have been watching you. We know all there is to know about you.". The first two bytes are message header fields; inline formatting is interpreted by $67B7.

Headered sequence message 4, selected through $8ED4/$8EDB by $8E09. Normalized visible text in the captured setup: "We even know of your weaknesses.". The first two bytes are message header fields; inline formatting is interpreted by $67B7.

Headered sequence message 5, selected through $8ED4/$8EDB by $8E09. Normalized visible text in the captured setup: "These weaknesses have made you my thrall.". The first two bytes are message header fields; inline formatting is interpreted by $67B7.

Headered sequence message 6, selected through $8ED4/$8EDB by $8E09. Normalized visible text in the captured setup: "To regain your freedom you must vanquish me in my castle at the heart of the Labyrinth.". The first two bytes are message header fields; inline formatting is interpreted by $67B7.

Continuation of the seventh headered message beginning at $8FDE, through its terminator at $903F. Its visible text continues with the requirement to vanquish the speaker in the castle at the heart of the Labyrinth.
